summary: Collections can depend on specific ansible-core, Python, Python package, system package and other collection versions, which can conflict; virtualenvs only partially solve this.
questions: Why do my Ansible collections have conflicting dependencies?
Are Python virtualenvs enough to isolate Ansible dependencies?
What kinds of dependencies do collections have?

answer_card.title: Dependency problems EEs solve
answer_card.answer_md: Collections can depend on specific versions of `ansible-core`, Python, Python packages, system packages and other collections. Installing these with RPM or pip on the host can lead to conflicts. Python virtual environments only **partially** fix this and have their own limits, which is a key reason to use Execution Environments.
